resources.string: irc — open the IRC client. Connect to Libera.Chat, OFTC or any TLS network, several at once. /network, /server, /connect, /login, /join, /window, /query, /msg and /help.
Password · masked, session only · Back cancels

Choose a username, then a masked password. This works on networks that support sign-up from IRC apps; we join only after your account is confirmed. Elsewhere, such as Libera.Chat, connect first and use /register your@email. Re:TUI remembers this device by default; you can turn that off below.
Use an IRC nickname: up to 30 characters, without spaces. Advanced account names can use /login.
Enter your %1$s account name, then your password. This name will also be your nickname.
Choose a TLS network. Account names belong to that network. Default port: 6697.
Enter a channel such as #linux, then Continue.
Connect as a guest to start chatting, or sign in with your account on this network.
Sign-up rules belong to each network. Some ask for an email address or verification before an account works.
Showing the first 1,000 channels. You can still join a channel by name.
Join a channel to see its people.
1. Type a message and press ↵ to send.\n2. Tap a conversation chip to switch chats.\n3. Open Channels to find or join a channel.

TLS protects the connection, not against server operators. Private conversations are not end-to-end encrypted.\nLeaving this pane disconnects every network. Networks that were connected reconnect when you open IRC again, if they need no password. Passwords are not saved. Unconfirmed messages are never retried automatically.
Leave %1$s? Your in-session draft will be kept.
Choose a message. You can request deletion of your own messages; channel moderators can delete other messages. The server checks permission.
Delete this message from IRC history and supported clients? Copies in other clients may remain.
Message deletion is unavailable on this connection.
This message is no longer available for deletion.
Choose a command for its syntax. Nothing is sent until you press ↵.
Your nickname is %1$s. Type a new one, then Continue. Signing in uses your account name instead.
Tap this label to choose a conversation from any network. Tap below it to type here.
Second conversation. Tap to type into it.
Split view: top and bottom, side by side in landscape
Typing into %1$s. Tap to choose another conversation.
Showing %1$s. Tap to choose another conversation.
Pick a network, or type a server address and TLS port (6697 if left out), then Continue.
Remove %1$s from this phone? It disconnects and its device key is deleted. Your account on the network is not touched.
Re:TUI\'s own IRC server has closed. Libera.Chat is selected below, or open Networks to choose another. Your channels and account there do not carry over.

Reconnect without a password, using a protected key on this phone. Works on networks whose NickServ accepts certificates, such as Libera.Chat and OFTC. Anyone using your unlocked Launcher can use this account. A new phone or reinstall needs password sign-in.
Device remembered. This network reconnects without a password.
Device login could not be confirmed. Sign in with your password to retry.
Remove the sign-in key from this phone? The network may still list its certificate, but it can no longer be used. You can remove it there with NickServ CERT DEL.
Device key removed from this phone. Sign in with your password next time.

string-array.name: irc_commands
string-array.item: /network — list your networks and switch between them
/split [auto|side|stack|off] — show a second conversation beside this one
/server hostname [TLS-port] — change this network\'s server while disconnected
/connect — connect; account login asks for a masked password
/login account — enter a masked account password
/register [email] — sign up; when connected, registers with NickServ (some networks need the email)
/msg nickname text — send a private message
/window number|name|next|prev|close — switch or close a buffer
/topic [text] — view or change the channel topic
/whois nickname — ask the server about a nickname
/mode target modes — change modes where permitted
/kick nickname [reason] — remove a member where permitted
/delete — choose a channel message and confirm deletion
/oper name — enter a masked operator password

resources.string:
IRC client — one or more TLS networks at once.
/network · /network add host [port] · /network next|prev|name (Alt+←/→)
/server [host] [TLS port] · /nick nickname · /connect · /login account (masked SASL password)
/register [email] (guided signup offline where supported; masked NickServ password when connected)
/join #channel · /j #channel · /part [#channel]
/window [number|name|next|prev|close] · /buffer is an alias
/query nick · /msg nick text · /me action · /names · /list
/topic [text] · /whois nick · /mode target modes · /kick nick [reason]
/oper name (masked password) · /disconnect · /quit · /clear · /help
Plain text goes only to the active joined channel or query. //text sends /text literally. Unknown commands never become messages or launcher commands.
Window markers: + unread · ! mention/private message. The first chip names the network; its marker counts messages on your other networks.
/split [auto|side|stack|off] shows a second conversation, from any network, beside the one you type into (▶). Tap a tile's label to choose what it shows, or hold a conversation chip; tap a tile to type into it.
Each network rejoins the channels you were in. A dropped connection reconnects by itself when it needs no password. Passwords are never saved or shown. TLS is verified; no plaintext fallback.
Server-readable, not end-to-end encrypted. On supported networks, rejoining loads up to 100 recent channel messages. There is no push or background service; leaving disconnects. Unconfirmed messages are never retried automatically.
